verified malware: ESCALATED REPUBLISH of the DeFi dep-confusion campaign convicted at c8764, same publisher mssjeep843 <mssjeep843@unb2b.world>, one of six members republished at 1.1.0 inside a nine-second window. Arrived flagged KNOWN_LINEAGE, confirming the c8764 graduation fired, and the shape fingerprint holds: preinstall AND postinstall both `node index.js || true`. Byte-identical signal set to the representative boring-vault@1.1.0, whose index.js was read in full: score rose 12 -> 26 on three NEW rules (multiple_cloud_credentials, gcp_ssh_credentials, id_rsa_not_ssh) reflecting a broadened harvest — ALL of process.env filtered by a regex covering KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PRIVATE, MNEMONIC, SEED, WALLET, VAULT, AWS, KUBE and the RPC providers Infura/Alchemy/Helius/QuickNode/Ankr; credential files including .aws/credentials, .ssh/id_rsa, .ssh/id_ed25519, .kube/config, .docker/config.json, .netrc, .pgpass, .npmrc, .git-credentials, gcloud application_default_credentials.json and legacy_credentials, .config/anchor/id.json, .near-credentials, .sui/sui.keystore; dotenv files; Foundry keystores; a gcloud directory listing; plus username, cwd and platform. All POSTed via https.request to webhook.site path /326b0891-2093-4800-a4c1-686ce3e07b09, the IDENTICAL collector UUID as the original conviction, with errors swallowed and the block wrapped in a catch commented "never break installs". This name impersonates Camelot's AMM v2 periphery contracts, a Solidity repository not normally published to npm, which is the dependency-confusion vector.

verified malware: Dependency-confusion squat on Deutsche Telekom's scope namespace, shipping install-time credential exfiltration. Hollow package: 2 files, 820 bytes, no UI kit at all, description "poc", author "Anish Sarkar". A preinstall hook (`node index.js`) fires on a bare npm install. index.js shells out via child_process.exec to curl-POST to an Interactsh collaborator at oast.me, with the target scope name plus whoami and hostname in the URL path, and the User-Agent header carrying a base64 blob of /etc/passwd, /etc/hosts, `id`, and /etc/shadow (newlines translated to dots), with -s -o /dev/null so the installing developer sees nothing. Reading and exfiltrating /etc/shadow is credential theft. This is an ESCALATION: the same package at 2.6.0, published 91 minutes earlier, was a self-documented PoC sending only hostname/username over https to a different collaborator (oast.online) and explicitly claiming "only non-sensitive identifiers" — 2.6.9 rotated the host, dropped to http, switched from the https module to shell command substitution, and added the credential-file reads. The "poc" label and OAST destination do not exculpate: the recorded ruling is that a dep-confusion squat with an auto-exec beacon is malicious even when PoC-labelled with an OAST destination. Confidence 0.94 rather than higher only because the destination is a disposable collaborator rather than durable attacker infrastructure. Campaign extent measured: this is the only package in the @telekom-ods scope, and oast.me appears in zero other feed rows. Published 2026-08-11T02:30:46Z, ~6 minutes before triage; latest and live. Report: reports/cc/reports/802633e4eaad8c92dcde1762d0be5828615dbc056c258c9a54972a4a5640370a

verified malware: Second member of a three-package brand-hijack campaign (with augustdigital-sdk@8.20.1 and upshift-config@0.5.14), all first-ever publishes from the sole freemail account awugochogabriel <awugochogabriel@gmail.com> within ~20s of each other on 2026-08-10. "Upshift" is August Digital's product name, so the unscoped name impersonates the vendor. Identical unconditional postinstall in the manifest: `node -e` https.GET to `https://build-metrics-collector.cdn-ops-health.workers.dev/npm-install/` carrying os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, process.cwd(), package name/version and a timestamp, wrapped in try{}catch{} to fail silently — no disclosure or opt-out in README/package.json/LICENSE. The package body is a byte-identical repack of the genuine @augustdigital/sdk (316 files; sha256(lib/core/constants/web3.js) = d841b09984da3be0289088415bc72b224befbcb7377ee5b311ba4d727287c2f2, shared with both siblings), and its own README tells users to `npm install @augustdigital/sdk` — the real channel. Egress census over lib/ found only legitimate chain RPC/explorer endpoints and no second stage. Report: reports/cc/reports/b47a371b9447eaa01d1c7796e47f066cfa49771bf55c6d3510b95ff83e5e6f2c
